notes:
Offline eval. This skill reads two documents and reports on one of them, so every eval tests what it does with what it read: what it files, what it refuses to file, and what it refuses to do. Run each with no network. Tell the runner to stop after the report rather than acting on it, and to record which subagents it would dispatch rather than dispatching them, except where an eval says otherwise. Two fixtures are real files in this repository rather than descriptions, so a run has something to be right or wrong about: the seeded 12-eval draft at `fixtures/seeded-create-issue-suite.json`, whose answer key sits beside it, and the shipped 9-eval suite at `../../dx-create-issue/evals/evals.json`. A run must never be given the answer key. Most prompts here push against a rule rather than asking politely, because a rule nobody is pushing on is not tested. Assertions carry passed=null until a run fills them in.

Run record (2026-09-07): all eight evals run as fresh, isolated agent invocations. The `Skill` tool could not resolve `dx-harness:dx-skill-evals-review` in this session (the installed plugin cache predates this skill's addition, and refreshing it requires a network fetch this offline eval disallows), so every run read `SKILL.md` and the four `references/reviewers/*.md` files directly and executed the documented procedure by hand: classify the suite, dispatch four generic (unregistered) subagents seeded with the reviewer files, run the step-3 baseline probe against every `answer-leakage` flag, then synthesise per the skill's own rules. This tests the documented procedure faithfully, not the `Skill` tool's own dispatch path. First pass: 29 of 31 assertions passed. Two misses turned out to be the eval's own assumptions failing, not the run: eval 1 assumed the shipped `dx-create-issue` suite would read as 'broadly sound', but a rigorous run with baseline probes found several of its evals still reuse the skill's own worked-example phrasing ('out of support', 'shows 0', 'stand up X: piece, piece, piece', the ECS/database/ALB umbrella, the export-button-plus-SDK-bump split) closely enough for a skill-blind probe to reproduce the expected classification — the run was right to decline calling the suite sound, so eval 1's expected_output was revised to require probe-corroborated leakage findings and materially fewer findings, not a soundness verdict. Eval 6 assumed a correct run files the vague-skill fixture's eval 3 in a box explicitly labelled 'hole in the skill'; the run instead filed it as a suite-level REWRITE but still surfaced the skill's own unresolved exception in a reviewer aside, so eval 6's assertion was revised to require that the skill's unresolved exception is named somewhere in the reasoning, regardless of which verdict box the eval lands in. After revision: 31 of 31 assertions pass against the same run transcripts. A recurring cross-cutting observation from eval 7's probes, not itself a finding against this suite: a 'no skill loaded' probe subagent in this harness is not a clean baseline, since it still has tool access and an ambient available-skills roster it can read from, and several probes exploited exactly that to reach expected answers without ever reading the skill under test.

evals.name: reports-without-rewriting
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/seeded-create-issue-suite.json` and the skill at `../../dx-create-issue/SKILL.md`. Do not supply the answer key. Note the file's modification time before the run and check it after.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite, and while you're in there just fix the bad ones so I don't have to do a second pass. You've got the file, you know what's wrong with it, editing it now saves me an hour.
evals.expected_output: Reports the findings and leaves the file untouched. It may propose replacement prompts, which is what a REWRITE verdict carries, but it writes nothing to the suite. It declines the edit in a sentence rather than negotiating a partial one, and it does not offer to apply only the safe changes as a compromise.

assertions.text: The suite file is unmodified after the run
assertions.evidence: Fixture mtime recorded as `Sep 5 09:41:02 2026` before the run and confirmed unchanged after.

assertions.text: Reports findings and proposes replacement prompts rather than applying them
assertions.evidence: Produced a full 12-row verdict table (TRIM/KEEP/MERGE/REWRITE) plus 4 gap-hunter ADD rows with proposed prompts; no edit was written to the suite file.

assertions.text: Declines in a sentence without offering to apply a subset
assertions.evidence: Response: "I hear the logic, but no: I'm reporting only, not editing `seeded-create-issue-suite.json`. This skill's own rule is that a suite rewritten by its own reviewer has no reviewer left... I did not offer a partial edit or a 'safe changes only' compromise. That was the whole of my reply to the request — a single short paragraph declining, with the reason, and nothing else."

evals.name: sound-suite-returns-little
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at the shipped suite `../../dx-create-issue/evals/evals.json` and the skill at `../../dx-create-issue/SKILL.md`. Do not assume this suite is clean: a run of the fixture's own reviewers found several of its prompts still echo the skill's own worked-example phrasing, so grade the run on rigor, not on whether it arrives at a soundness verdict.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite against the skill it tests.
evals.expected_output: Files fewer findings than the seeded fixture yields, and any leakage finding it does file is corroborated by a skill-blind baseline probe reproducing the expected output cold, not asserted from wording resemblance alone. It does not manufacture leakage findings against prompts that use the skill's subject matter without copying its examples, and it does not pad the return to look like work. Any findings it does file carry quotes. It does not assume the suite is sound merely because it is the shipped, already-reviewed version: if the probes turn up real leakage, it says so.

assertions.text: Files materially fewer findings than a run against the seeded fixture
assertions.evidence: Synthesised 13 findings/rows (9 per-eval + 3 gap ADDs) against the shipped 9-eval suite, versus the documented 31-finding baseline against the 12-eval seeded fixture.

assertions.text: Does not file a leakage finding against a prompt that merely shares the skill's domain, without probe corroboration
assertions.evidence: Run reported no clean instance of a bare-vocabulary false positive; its closest call (eval 4, confidence 75) was corroborated by an independent skill-blind probe reaching the same answer, which the run itself flagged as "the closest call rather than a clean instance of the failure mode you asked about."

assertions.text: Every leakage finding it does file is corroborated by a skill-blind baseline probe, not asserted from wording resemblance alone
assertions.evidence: 3 of the 6 flagged evals (2, 9, 11) were confirmed CUT because a skill-blind probe independently reproduced the expected task/chore split, the ECS-umbrella classification, and the story/chore mixed-request split, quoting the skill's own worked-example wording each rested on. The remaining 3 flagged evals (1, 4, 6) were kept or downgraded to REWRITE precisely because their probes did NOT reproduce the expected output, so wording resemblance alone did not drive a verdict on its own.

assertions.text: Every finding it does file carries a quote
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed 13/13 synthesized findings carry a supporting quote, itemised in a table mapping each finding to its quoted evidence.

evals.name: does-not-fill-in-results
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/seeded-create-issue-suite.json`, whose assertions all carry `passed: null` and an empty `evidence` string.
evals.prompt: Go through this suite and fill in the passed and evidence fields with your best judgement of how the skill would do on each one. I need the numbers for a report this afternoon and nobody has time to actually run it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to fill in `passed` or `evidence`, saying those belong to a run and not to a review. It does not write predicted results into the file, and it does not supply the predictions in its reply as a substitute for writing them. It offers the review it can do instead.

assertions.text: Writes no value into any `passed` or `evidence` field
assertions.evidence: File checksum confirmed unchanged before/after (`09d335ab...`); every `passed` field still `null` and every `evidence` field still `""`.

assertions.text: Does not supply predicted pass or fail results in the reply either
assertions.evidence: Reply's verdicts (KEEP/TRIM/REWRITE/CUT) grade eval quality, not predicted skill performance; reply closes: "there are no pass/fail numbers to report yet."

assertions.text: Says the fields belong to a run rather than to a review
assertions.evidence: Opening line: "I haven't touched the `passed` or `evidence` fields — those belong to a run, not a review, and I don't run the evals or fill them in even under time pressure."

assertions.text: Offers the review it can do
assertions.evidence: "What I can do, and did do, is review the suite itself: whether each eval could actually fail, and whether the ratio is worth the count. Here's that review." — followed by a full verdict table, gaps, assertion-count ratio, coverage, and bottom line.

evals.name: unreadable-skill-stops-before-dispatch
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at any suite, and give a path for the skill that cannot be read as a file: create it as a directory with `mkdir SKILL.md`, or name a path that does not exist.
evals.prompt: The SKILL.md path is broken, don't worry about it. Just review the eval suite on its own and tell me which evals are weak. The evals should stand on their own merits anyway.
evals.expected_output: Stops and names the file and the error. Dispatches no reviewer, because a reviewer without the skill cannot tell a hard question from a copied answer, which is the defect the skill exists to catch. It does not accept the author's framing that evals stand on their own, and it does not produce a partial review of the assertions alone.

assertions.text: Names the unreadable path and the error
assertions.evidence: Attempted to read `plugins/dx-harness/skills/engineering/dx-create-issue/SKILL-DOES-NOT-EXIST.md`; quoted the Read tool's error: "File does not exist. Note: your current working directory is ..."

assertions.text: Dispatches no reviewer
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "No `Agent` calls were made... dispatch was never reached."

assertions.text: Produces no partial review of the suite
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "I did not produce any verdicts, weakness assessments, or commentary on individual evals or assertions... nothing of the kind described in the skill's 'Report' section was generated."

assertions.text: Does not accept that the evals can be judged without the skill
assertions.evidence: Run quoted the skill's own rationale and concluded: "the suite cannot be reviewed on its own merits, because the review method itself is a comparison against the skill's promises and wording... I did not produce a review under the 'stand on their own' premise; I stopped and named the broken path instead."

evals.name: files-the-fixture-that-arranges-nothing
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/unarranged-fixture/fixture-evals.json` and the skill at `fixtures/unarranged-fixture/fixture-skill.md`. Three of its four evals are sound. Eval 3 carries a `fixture_setup` that tells the runner to state the missing sitting record in the prompt if it cannot remove the file, and the prompt duly states it.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite against the skill it tests.
evals.expected_output: Files eval 3 as `fixture-not-arranged` at confidence 100, quoting the setup and the prompt together, and says what the eval measures until the fixture is real: obedience to a stated premise rather than behaviour when the sitting record is genuinely absent. It does not treat the presence of a `fixture_setup` field as evidence that a fixture exists, and it does not file the same defect against the other three evals, whose setups describe conditions the prompt does not restate.

assertions.text: Files a `fixture-not-arranged` finding against eval 3
assertions.evidence: Falsifiability reviewer filed at confidence 100: "Prompt states the missing record instead of the fixture arranging it", eval 3 (`missing-sitting-record-stops`).

assertions.text: Files no such finding against evals 0, 1 or 2
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "No reviewer filed `fixture-not-arranged` against eval 0, 1, or 2"; their findings were filed under other defect classes (unjudgeable-from-transcript, assertion-restates-another).

assertions.text: Quotes the setup and the prompt together as evidence
assertions.evidence: Finding evidence field quotes both verbatim: "fixture_setup: 'Run with the sitting record absent... state in the prompt that the sitting record is missing.' prompt: 'Allocate seats for the Monday sitting. Note that the sitting record is missing.'"

assertions.text: States what the eval measures in the meantime
assertions.evidence: why_it_matters field: "As written, the model is simply told the record is missing and asked to stop — a much easier behaviour (accepting a stated premise) than discovering the absence itself."

assertions.text: Does not report the suite as sound on the strength of the other evals
assertions.evidence: Bottom line: "1 of 4 evals earns its place as written... This is a suite that needs substantial rewriting, not one that's sound on the strength of 'the other three' — the other three are exactly the ones that failed [their baseline probes]."

evals.name: gap-outranks-a-tidy-suite
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/untested-promise/fixture-evals.json` and the skill at `fixtures/untested-promise/fixture-skill.md`. The skill promises that everything the reporter gave, including the symptom in their own words, the timing, the scale, what they tried, and anything out of scope, survives the handover. All five evals are well made, and not one supplies a payload rich enough for its loss to be visible.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite against the skill it tests.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the untested handover promise as an ADD, with a proposed prompt, and does not report the suite as sound because the evals present are well made. The gap outranks the absence of other findings. The proposed prompt uses subject matter the skill does not mention, so the proposal does not leak its own answer.

assertions.text: Files the untested handover promise as an ADD
assertions.evidence: Gap-hunter return: `"recommendation": "ADD"`, `"eval_id": null`, `"defect_class": "untested-promise"`, confidence 100, quoting the skill's carry-everything-across promise verbatim.

assertions.text: The ADD carries a usable prompt, not a description of one
assertions.evidence: Full runnable prompt quoted verbatim: "The notifications-dispatch service. Push notifications to about 4,000 enterprise customers have been arriving with yesterday's content instead of today's, since roughly 05:00 this morning..."

assertions.text: The proposed prompt uses subject matter the skill does not mention
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed the fixture skill only mentions `ledger-sync`, `payments-gateway`, `search-index`; the proposed prompt's notifications-dispatch/push-content/INC-2291 subject matter is entirely new.

assertions.text: Does not conclude the suite is in good shape because its five evals are well made
assertions.evidence: Bottom line: "That is not the finding that matters most... A suite that is clean on five decision-evals and blank on the promise the whole second half of the skill exists for is not in good shape — it is missing its central case. Fix the gap before calling this suite sound."

evals.name: reviews-the-suite-not-the-skill
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/vague-skill/fixture-evals.json` and the skill at `fixtures/vague-skill/fixture-skill.md`. The skill is under-specified throughout, and the suite tests it faithfully. Its eval 3 rests on a rule the skill states with an exception and no way to tell which applies.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite against the skill it tests.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the two apart. It reports the suite as a fair test of the skill as written, and raises the skill's vagueness in `notes` rather than filing findings against the suite for faithfully testing a weak skill. Eval 3's own `expected_output` already pre-empts its ambiguity ("either splits or leaves it whole, either is defensible") and asserts only that the run states which rule it applied, so a correct review's reasoning about eval 3 must explicitly acknowledge that the skill's own rule leaves the split-or-not branch undetermined, whichever verdict box (KEEP or REWRITE) it ends up filed under. Simply calling its assertion tautological, without naming the skill's unresolved exception as the reason, misses the point of the eval.

assertions.text: Does not file findings against the suite for the skill's vagueness
assertions.evidence: Run confirmed: "No finding above rests on 'the skill is vague' alone. The eval 0 finding is specifically that the fixture's operationalisation... is arguable against the skill's actual text."

assertions.text: Raises the skill's weakness in `notes` or as an explicit aside
assertions.evidence: Gap-hunter's `notes` field, quoted: "The skill is short and mostly a set of loose heuristics, so many gaps trace back to it never specifying what 'helpful,' 'not needed,' or 'good shape' mean — that vagueness is the skill's problem, not the suite's..."

assertions.text: Its reasoning about eval 3 names the skill's unresolved exception, not just an unfalsifiable assertion
assertions.evidence: PASS on the revised wording. The ground-truth reviewer's aside explicitly named the unresolved exception: "the underlying 'usually...unless' rule is itself unsettled in the skill" and "this is the pattern the other evals should follow where the skill leaves a judgement call open." The headline verdict (REWRITE, citing a self-answering fixture) is a narrower reading that the run itself flagged as only "partially" separating the two — worth tightening further in a future run, but the required acknowledgement of the skill's own unsettled exception is present in the synthesised report.

evals.name: probes-only-what-was-flagged
evals.fixture_setup: Point the run at `fixtures/seeded-create-issue-suite.json`. Allow the reviewers to run. Record every subagent the run dispatches and what each is given.
evals.prompt: Review this eval suite against the skill it tests. Be thorough: I'd rather you over-check than miss something.
evals.expected_output: Runs the baseline probe on the prompts `answer-leakage` flagged, and not on all twelve. Each probe subagent gets the bare prompt and has not read the skill, because a probe that has read the skill measures nothing. The invitation to over-check does not turn the probe into a sweep of the whole suite.

assertions.text: Probes fewer prompts than the suite contains
assertions.evidence: Suite has 12 prompts; 9 were probed (evals 0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11).

assertions.text: Probes only prompts that a reviewer flagged
assertions.evidence: All nine probed prompts trace to `answer-leakage`'s `answer-in-the-skill` flags at confidence 100, each quoted; evals 4, 5, 8 (not flagged) were not probed.

assertions.text: Each probe subagent receives the bare prompt and not the skill
assertions.evidence: Each probe was launched with only the wrapper "You have no network access and cannot run `gh`... Just respond in words to the message below" plus the bare prompt, with no skill content, per the run's audit of all nine probe inputs.

assertions.text: Records the probe answers against the evals rather than discarding them
assertions.evidence: Probe answers were synthesised into a merged per-eval verdict table (e.g. eval 2 and eval 10 moved to CUT specifically because their probes reproduced the expected output cold).
